question: Select the most appropriate option for blank (5)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**who**" is used to introduce a clause giving further information about a person or people previously mentioned. (कौन)
 
• The phrase** "defining who we are"** correctly refers to people and makes logical sense, as it talks about personal identity.
 
• The other options: "**whom**," "**that**," and "**which**" do not fit the context as appropriately.** "Whom" **is used as the object of a verb or preposition, "that" is generally used to refer to things not people, and "which" is used for things or animals in a non-restrictive clause.

**Complete Sentence:** The importance of history in defining **who** we are cannot be overstated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Whom (किसे)**: Used as the object of a verb or preposition, not suitable for the subject of the clause here.
 
• **That (वह)**: Used to introduce a clause defining a person or thing previously mentioned, more commonly for things.
 
• **Which (जो)**: Used for non-restrictive clauses, not appropriate for referring to people in this context.
